title: The Great Depression
text: The Great Depression was the most severe global economic downturn of the 20th century, beginning with the U.S. stock market crash of October 1929 and lasting until the late 1930s. GDP fell by 30% in the United States, and unemployment reached 25% at its peak. Banks failed in large numbers, wiping out savings. The Depression spread worldwide, affecting virtually all countries. President Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal (1933–1939) introduced programs including Social Security, the FDIC (bank deposit insurance), and public works projects. The Depression ended primarily as countries began rearmament spending in the late 1930s and early 1940s, which boosted employment.
